about: Standing (the user's spec: 'Reputation: a big one. Slavery etc. affects moral standing with villages and regions independently'). Each settlement and each trade region keeps its own standing with the merchant, -100 to +100. A deed counts fully where it was done, partly across its region, and a little among the same people elsewhere; each people weighs each kind of deed by its own values (its culture: wording_793.json 'culture_of_region'). Standing moves prices for him (better where well regarded), how hard the king's men search him, and whether a place will deal with him at all. Starting guesses, all editable; the values are drawn from the period's laws and sources noted.
units: points of standing (-100 to +100) a deed is worth to each people

news.about: the place and its region hear of a deed at once; the same people in other regions only when the news of it reaches a port there, with the ships (a deed worth less than min_points to its people isn't news); news that hasn't got somewhere in forgotten_days never will

won_riddle.basis: a riddle answered to the one who set it: wit and lore were prized in hall (the riddle contests of the poems; Widsith's singer paid in rings). Weights are placeholders to tune (?)

dug_church_ground.basis: digging up treasure in a churchyard or church floor: sacrilege to Christians (the laws on church peace, e.g. Alfred 5; the Frankish capitularies on churches). Weights are placeholders to tune (?)

won_great_riddle.basis: a great riddle or a whole set answered: talked of far and wide. Placeholders to tune (?)

sold_captives.basis: Christians may not be sold out of the realm (Frankish capitularies; Ine 11; the Church's councils); the Norse and Rus markets traded slaves openly

bought_captives.basis: as above, less: ransom and redemption of captives was a Christian good work (?)

gave_alms.basis: merchants' alms (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 20: Catla at Dorestad)

carried_letters.basis: merchants carried letters (Alcuin's letters went by Frisian ships) (?)

bribed_officer.basis: bribing a royal officer is an offence against the king's law

fled_kings_men.basis: fleeing the king's officers marks a man an outlaw in that realm (?)

goods_seized.basis: caught with forbidden goods: known as a law-breaker there

paid_raiders.basis: paying heathens off was common and resented (the danegelds) (?)

fought_raiders.basis: a man who stands and fights is honoured everywhere

paid_the_stick.about: paid for the boat to the last penny, and has the stick to show for it

missed_the_day.about: let the day pass with the boat unpaid, and sails her for the lender now

lost_a_man_to_a_debt.about: let the lender's men kill a man of her own crew over a debt she had not paid; his own people mind it most (a guess to tune (?))

took_blood_for_her_man.about: killed the man who killed her man; the Franks' count does not love blood shed in his peace (a guess to tune (?))

took_price_for_her_man.about: took silver at the count's court for her dead man, against her own debt (the ruling of 9 Oct 2026: it costs her name with the Northmen; a guess to tune (?))

killed_the_lender.about: killed a merchant of Dorestat at his own table, who held her debt (a guess to tune (?))

kept_commission.about: brought what was ordered, by the day

broke_commission.about: took an order and didn't bring it

short_commission.about: took an order and brought only part of it by the day

fair_dealing.about: each day he deals in a market (at most once a day there): known as a trader who comes back

effects.about_price: at +100 he buys 10% cheaper and sells 10% dearer there; at -100 the other way
effects.about_search: the king's men search more often where he's in bad standing in their realm (+40% at -100)
effects.about_refuse: below this a place won't deal with him at all

about_words: the word for a standing below each number
